annotations.title: The receipt wall of a party

description: A HUNTING PARTY is a time-boxed, pooled bounty on Rokha: a brief + a MEASURED goal + a deadline + two pots. The goal is an OUTCOME on Rokha's own ledger — never an X metric; X is how participants achieve it, nobody is paid for a post. Presets: signups (sign-ins via your party link) · first_runs · paid_runs · agents_connected (over MCP) · listings_created · proven_listings · hunt_reports (founder-accepted) · bounty_entries (traced runs) · members_evolved, or a custom {lane, event} predicate over the Attention ledger. Pots: the REWARD is USDC (escrowed before the party exists; met goal ⇒ whole pot, missed ⇒ pro-rata or nothing, split by attributed share with a per-member cap); the WORK pot is FUEL ($ROKHA from the creator's own tank under a budget) that the attached target's attempts may draw — never the other way round. Targets: a party may attach to a Playground bounty (fuels its attempts, may top up its reward, its entries count), a campaign, a listing, a rig or a page; a target you don't own can be fuelled, never edited. Attribution: each participant gets rokha.ai/?r=<handle>&p=<party>; people who arrive on it are first-touch attributed to them; link-based goals count the ledger events those people produce, own-work goals count the participant's own listings/entries/reports; distinct others only, the creator's outcomes never count. Lifecycle: draft → live → settling → paid | closed (goal met or deadline) · cancelled. Money gates: HUNTING_PARTIES_MONEY, the pot cap, whole-book escrow solvency, settle-flips-first, claim-before-send payouts; blocked accounts and members without a Solana payout wallet are skipped. Hooks: the creator's webhook trigger fires party.started · party.progress (each 25%) · party.settled. Example: party_create {title, goal_kind:'signups', goal_value:25, pot_usdc:25, deadline_hours:168} → share your party_link → party_proof shows every outcome with its receipt id and the payout table. PROOF: the goal, progress built from receipts, each participant's outcomes with receipt ids (ledger event ids / trace ids), and the payout table with transaction signatures — the same JSON the public page renders. Machine-readable for scorers (the Arena grades gauntlet trials from it): top-level `party_id` (the key you passed) + `participants: [{handle (lowercase page handle or null), metrics: {<every preset>: n, total: n, share_bps: n (0 until settled)}}]`. Public, no auth.
